answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake bonded to a verified work history before it may trade. Reputation is a single thread running through every deal: a new identity enters through one narrow inlet, with no history and a capped stake, so it cannot flood the market. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts achieves nothing, because each sock puppet must lock real funds and build a slow, checkable record before earning trust, making a thousand fake identities cost a thousand stakes.
